derivation: code-derived: every mutant is drawn from a decision in the source under test (the SKIP tuple, the path-normalisation, and the classifier's two clauses), never from reading the cases and asking what would break them
sweep: one sequential sweep, .agents/scripts/tests/ patched on disk and restored in a finally; residue checked afterwards (no `return True`, no inverted classifier, git status shows only the intended edits)
result: 6/6 killed, each by its DECLARED case

mutants.decision_mutated: is_skipped() matches the path against the SKIP markers
mutants.mutant: widen the skip to every path (return True)

mutants.decision_mutated: scan_path() normalises to a ROOT-relative path before matching
mutants.mutant: match the ABSOLUTE path instead (return f.as_posix())
mutants.note: this is the trap the marker creates and the reason the normalisation exists: a lane checkout LIVES at <root>/.claude/worktrees/<lane>/, so an absolute match would skip every file of a lane run and report a vacuous clean scan of nothing

mutants.mutant: drop the errno clause (excuse any admin-directory failure)

width_note: M4 and M5 are the two NARROWING mutants the rule asks for: each drops one arm of a two-clause AND, and each is caught by a control string that exercises exactly the arm that was dropped - one naming the admin directory with a git errno (File exists), one carrying our errno on a different path (/tmp/x). Without both control strings the two clauses would be certified only jointly, which is the boundary a real regression walks through.
